exposure: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (gestational hypertension, preeclampsia)
outcome: Infant growth outcomes (birth weight z-scores, birth length z-scores, 6-month weight z-scores, 2-year weight z-scores, change in weight z-scores, rapid weight gain, conditional weight gain z-scores)
cohort: Infants born to women enrolled in the prospective Postpartum Physiology, Psychology and Paediatric (P4) cohort study who experienced normotensive pregnancy, gestational hypertension, or preeclampsia.
finding: Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia were associated with accelerated infant weight gain from birth to 2 years, potentially increasing future cardiometabolic disease risk, despite preeclampsia-exposed infants being smaller at birth.
birth_weight: Measured as z-scores; PE-exposed infants had significantly lower birth weight z-scores compared to NTP or GH-exposed infants.
gest_age: Measured; small for gestational age was adjusted for as a confounder.
